The details of the legal heirs are mentioned in paragraph no. 1 of this application.

sentences.text:
4. Let the legal heirs, namely, Bharat Verma and Rajendra Verma, of deceased petitioner be substituted in place of the petitioner in course of the day by the learned counsel appearing for the applicants (legal heirs of the deceased petitioner).
5.
In the result, I.A No. 1 of 2025 stands allowed.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, learned counsel for the NHAI and learned counsel for the State have been heard on merit.

7. It is an admitted position that the petitioner's land detailed in the petition has been acquired and an award of Rs. 20,61,435.88/- was prepared and the same was paid to the petitioner by way of Annexure- 1 series, though, the petitioner accepted that award but he raised an objection by filing an application before the District Land Acquisition Officer, Katihar.
As per petitioner's counsel, he has not got any information about the decision on his objection petition till Patna High Court CWJC No.10332 of 2021(6) dt.04-09-2025 today.

As the issue raised by the petitioner with regard to quantum of compensation is to be determined by the Arbitrator as per the provisions of Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956, in view of the objection raised by the petitioner, so,
considering this aspect, the District Land Acquisition Officer/Collector of Katihar is hereby directed to refer the petitioner's application (Annexure-3) to the Arbitrator for taking a decision on his application, if the same is still with him.
The petitioner will also have a liberty to file a fresh application before the Arbitrator/ Divisional Commissioner, Purnea Division, to raise his grievance within four weeks from today.

Upon filing the fresh application or upon forwarding the petitioner's earlier objection petition by the Collector/Land Acquisition Officer, the Arbitrator shall decide the petitioner's application at the earliest as per the provisions of law.
8. Accordingly, with above direction the instant petition stands disposed of.
9. The period of time spent by the petitioner in this case shall be excluded by the Arbitrator while computing the necessary limitation period.

(Shailendra Singh, J) Rajiv/-
